To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the removal of reproductive sinks from a plant can induce the development of new sinks and the removal of the latter in turn can delay the senescence and increase the longevity of the plant.

removal of spikelets from the main panicle and emasculation of panicle by hot treatment delayed the senescence and increased the longevity of the main tillers and secondary and tertiary branches, which, in the end, increased the longevity of whole plant.
the spikelets of the rice plant are the major sink and that removal of spikelets delays the whole plant senesce.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of removal of different numbers of spikelets from the main tiller of rice plants and the emasculation of panicle on leaf senescence and longevity of the plant.
the effect of spikelet removal and emasculation on the whole plant longevity and senescence of IET 144, a nonsequential senescing rice plant.
the effect of spikelet removal and emasculation of rice panicle on the development of side branch and the senescence pattern of the whole plant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
removal of spikelets from the main panicle or emasculation by hot water treatment delayed senescence of leaves and the whole rice plant by inducing the development of secondary and tertiary branch.

the removal of spikelets from the main tiller, the secondary and the tertiary branch induces a sequential mode of leaf senescnce in all the tillers, and the removal of spikelet from the tertiary branch induces further side branches, which, in tur, delays the whole plant senecence.

the removal of 50, 75 and 80% spikelets of the panicle of main tiller and secondary branch induced secondary and tertiary branch development and delayed the leaf senescence and increased the whole plant longevity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

removal of spikelets from the main panicle or emasculation by hot water treatment induces the development of side branch from the axils of flag leaf, which, in its turn, produces side branch and so on, and the whole plant senesces sequentially.
the removal of spikelets (or emasculation) delays leaf senescence and prolongs the longevity of rice plant.
the development of secondary and tertiary side branches in rice plant is an adaptive mechanism for increasing longevity of the whole plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the removal of reproductive sinks can increase the longevity of the rice plant by delaying leaf senescence.

the spikelets of the rice plant are a sink for the assimilates of the whole plant and their removal or emasculation induces the production of additional sink (side branch), which, in turn controls the leaf senescence and longevity of the rice plant.
spikelet removal or emasculation can be used to delay leaf senescence in rice and thereby increase its longevity.
